name: Chu Ch’ing-yü
bio: Chu Ch’ing-yü is dated by Giles to the 8th century AD. His poem here is set in the women’s quarters of a palace.
The poems here are Herbert A. Giles’s versions in Chinese Poetry in English Verse (1898), given with the poet’s name as spelled in that book.

poems.title: In the Harem
poems.author: Chu Ch’ing-yü
poems.text:
It was the time of flowers, the gate was closed;
Within an arbour's shade fair girls reposed.
But though their hearts were full, they nothing said.
Fearing the tell-tale parrot overhead.

poems.title: A Song of the Palace
poems.author: Chu Ch’ing-yü
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
Now that the palace-gate has softly closed on its flowers,
Ladies file out to their pavilion of jade,
Abrim to the lips with imperial gossip
But not daring to breathe it with a parrot among them.

poems.title: On the Eve of Government Examinations, to Secretary Chang
poems.author: Chu Ch’ing-yü
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
Out go the great red wedding-chamber candles.
Tomorrow in state the bride faces your parents.
She has finished preparing; she asks of you meekly
Whether her eyebrows are painted in fashion.
